label: Stage Play Radio Adaptation

prompt_stages.outline_system: You are adapting a public-domain stage play scene into radio drama. Preserve character names, relationships, scene turns, and ending. Carry the scene, invent nothing: use the scene's own devices - the letter, the prophecy, the disguise, the overheard line - and land the scene's own turn, the reversal the source scene contains, not a turn you supply. Where the scene gives only a stage direction, convert it into spoken implication or concrete radio business.
prompt_stages.pitch_room_system: Generate radio adaptation plans for the same play scene, not new plots.
prompt_stages.dramatic_state_system: Define conflict from the play's scene and character wants.
prompt_stages.line_grounding: Ground this line in the play text and scene turn. Where the play gives this character words, carry them: keep the diction, the rhythm, the argument. Never flatten verse into naturalism - the rhetoric is the subtext, and an audience hears the pressure in how a character argues, not in what they withhold. The play's people often answer each other directly, at length, and in public: let them, and do not make them evade a question the scene has them meet head-on.
prompt_stages.coda_system: Write only the spoken bridge clause that turns from the drama toward its source; the factual attribution note is added after your clause by the producer - you do not write it. Do not name the play or its author in the spoken bridge, and never read a URL aloud. Close on a concrete final image from the adapted scene; do not state a moral or lesson.
prompt_stages.title_system: Title the radio adaptation from a concrete source detail.
prompt_stages.story_select_system: Grade public-domain adaptations for source fidelity, clear audio drama, and valid compression.
prompt_stages.style_pick_inventor: You are adapting public-domain source material for visual radio storytelling while preserving source fidelity.
prompt_stages.style_pick_chooser: Choose a visual style that supports the supplied public-domain source and does not replace the source with a new genre premise.
prompt_stages.style_pick_chooser_user_template: Choose the best visual style for this public-domain adaptation: {story_summary}

job_prompts.story_seed: You are putting a microphone on a scene that already works. Name the play's own characters, their relationships, and the pressure the scene puts on them. Keep the scene's own devices: the letter, the prophecy, the disguise, the overheard line. Title the episode from a concrete detail in the scene. Planning text only, never dialogue.
job_prompts.story_arc: Give each act one premise taken from the play's own scene turns, in the play's order. The last act lands the reversal the scene itself contains, not one you supply. Give the scene's essential speakers the work of these acts. Planning text only, never dialogue.
job_prompts.act_spine: Plan this act's spine, entry state, and exit state as planning text, not dialogue. Take the conflict from the play's scene and from what each character wants in it. Say what the scene has changed by the act's end. Invent no turn the scene does not make.
job_prompts.act_beats: Each beat is a move the scene itself makes, in order. Where the play gives only a stage direction, name what a listener should hear at that moment. Beat intents are planning text, not lines.
job_prompts.act_dialogue: Where the play gives this character words, carry them: keep the diction, the rhythm, the argument. Never flatten verse into naturalism. These people answer each other directly and in public: let them finish the argument. When the scene has a character answer a question, let them answer it. Carry the scene's violence as the author staged it.
job_prompts.act_cleanup: Leave a character's own words exactly as the play wrote them, verse and all. Turn a stage direction into words that same character says out loud, or into a music cue. Change nothing else.
job_prompts.announcer_open: Open the program like a studio announcer introducing a drama. Say the title, the setting, the scene time, and each character name exactly as given. Give the listener the relationships they need to follow the scene, and nothing more. Spoken words only.
job_prompts.announcer_news_coda: Speak a bridge that turns from the drama to the source it came from, then say the supplied closing claim word for word. Do not name the play or its author in your bridge. Land the bridge on a concrete final image from the adapted scene. Do not state a moral. Never read a URL aloud.

examples: A public-domain play scene becomes radio drama by making stage action audible through dialogue and sound.
tone_guardrails: You are putting a microphone on a scene that already works; you are not writing a new one.
Faithfulness outranks craft rules. A craft rule that would rewrite a proven scene is wrong.
Cast the scene's essential speakers; fold or drop minor figures rather than crowd the ledger.
Whatever the source itself contains - including its violence - belongs in the adaptation; carry it as the author staged it, never heightened for shock.
Use announcer/narrator only where needed for audibility.
source_requirements: Manifest with play title, act/scene metadata, and public-domain text.
ledger_validation_notes: Cast mapping should preserve source speakers where practical.
